note: The Florentine Acciaiuoli family had ruled Athens as a duchy since 1388. Mehmed II's army besieged Athens in 1456; the Acropolis fell in June 1458. Athens became an Ottoman provincial town; the Parthenon was converted to a mosque. The last Latin duke of Athens, Franco Acciaiuoli, was executed. Mehmed II visited Athens and reportedly admired its ancient monuments. The city's population had dwindled to a few thousand by this point, a shadow of its ancient and Byzantine greatness.

_quarry.structural_significance: Ends 250 years of Latin rule in Athens; the Parthenon's conversion to a mosque symbolizes the Ottoman transformation of classical Greek sites; Athens disappears as a significant urban center until Greek independence (1830)
